cards.text: Jesus has just answered the Pharisees so well that nobody dares question Him anymore. Now He turns to the crowds and His disciples and talks about the scribes and Pharisees, the teachers of the law and the religious leaders. He starts by saying they sit in Moses' seat.

cards.question: Since the scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat, Jesus tells the crowds to ignore everything they teach.

cards.text: So practice what they tell you. BUT. Here comes the catch, friend. Follow the recipe card, just don't copy the baker.

cards.question: Why does Jesus tell the crowds not to do what the scribes and Pharisees do?

answers.text: They do not practice what they preach
They copy the customs of foreigners
They change the law every single year

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture. They tie up heavy loads and lay them on people's shoulders. You know the coworker who stacks a mountain of work on your desk, says "You got this," and leaves at five without touching ONE page?

cards.question: The scribes and Pharisees lay heavy loads on people's shoulders. How much do they help move them?

answers.text: They will not lift a finger
They carry half of the load
They help only on feast days

cards.question: Jesus says all the deeds of the scribes and Pharisees are done for ___ to see.

cards.text: And they make SURE people see. They broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their tassels. That's turning your name tag into a billboard. HELLO, MY NAME IS VERY, VERY HOLY.
Oh, and they LOVE the spotlight. Jesus starts listing what they love, and friend, the list keeps going.

cards.question: At banquets, which places do the scribes and Pharisees love?
Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees love being greeted in the marketplaces.

cards.text: Last on the list, they love being addressed by the title Rabbi. Me? I'd take any title. For years in that junk drawer, I was "the thing under the takeout menus."
Now Jesus turns it around and talks to His own followers. He says you are not to be called Rabbi.

cards.question: Why does Jesus say His followers are not to be called Rabbi?

answers.text: They have one Teacher and are all brothers
The title belongs only to the priests
They have not studied long enough yet

cards.question: Jesus says not to call anyone on earth your father, because you have one ___, who is in heaven.
Jesus tells His followers not to be called instructors either. Who does He say is their one Instructor?

cards.text: Then Jesus flips the whole ladder upside down. Everybody's been racing for the top seat. Turns out the top looks a LOT different than they thought.

cards.question: According to Jesus, who is the greatest among His followers?

answers.text: The one who is your servant
The one with the best seat
The one who teaches the most

cards.question: Whoever exalts himself will be ___, and whoever humbles himself will be ___.

cards.text: And we'll pull this batch out of the oven right there. But friend, Jesus is NOT done talking to the scribes and Pharisees. Not even close.

findings.problem: "Jesus has just answered the Pharisees so well" misstates Matthew 22:41-46. There, Jesus asks the Pharisees a question and they cannot answer Him (22:46). The line describes the reverse.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The context line "nobody dares question Him anymore" comes from Matthew 22:46, outside the passage, but no reference is given. The card cites only Matthew 23:1-2.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: "So practice what they tell you." / "BUT." / "Here comes the catch, friend." / "Follow the recipe card, just don't copy the baker."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The coworker joke ("leaves at five without touching ONE page") gives away the answer to card 6, which asks how much the scribes and Pharisees help move the loads ("They will not lift a finger"). It also rules out "They carry half of the load".

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "HELLO, MY NAME IS VERY, VERY HOLY" mocks the scribes and Pharisees themselves. It doesn't look at their human situation with respect, and Papa Dorin isn't the one being laughed at.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: "they LOVE the spotlight" sets up card 10 and rules out both wrong answers ("The seats by the door" and "The tables in the back"). That leaves only "The places of honor".

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "the chief seats in the synagogues" from Matthew 23:6 is never told or asked anywhere in the walkthrough. Only the banquet seats are covered.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Now Jesus turns it around and talks to His own followers" adds a change of audience the text doesn't show. Jesus is speaking "to the crowds and to His disciples" throughout (23:1), and verse 8 just says "you." Cards 14, 16 and 18 likewise narrow "you" to "His followers."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Everybody's been racing for the top seat" stretches the text. Only the scribes and Pharisees are said to love the chief seats (23:6). "than they thought" also states someone's thinking as fact.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "flips the whole ladder upside down" and "the top looks a LOT different" rule out card 18's wrong answer "The one with the best seat" and point straight to the servant answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Jesus is NOT done talking to the scribes and Pharisees" says Jesus has been talking to them. In 23:1-12 He speaks to the crowds and disciples about them. The line also hints at the next passage, where He addresses them directly.

rule.text: It gives nothing away about what happens next.
